title: 1 day ago •INDYCAR Technologies INDYCAR Notebook: IR-28 Hits Road for Sebring Test Next Week The new IR-28 chassis (photo) will be tested at a track other than Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the first time Oct. 12-13.
excerpt:
INDYCAR Technologies

1 day ago

Testing of the new IR-28 chassis that will be introduced into the NTT INDYCAR SERIES at the start of the 2028 season will continue next week, with laps turned outside of Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the first time.

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou of Chip Ganassi Racing (photo, top) and 2016 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Alexander Rossi of ECR will continue to serve as drivers of the new car in testing Monday, Oct. 12 and Tuesday, Oct. 13 at Sebring International Raceway. Palou will test Monday, with Rossi taking over Tuesday.

The historic Florida circuit resembles conditions of INDYCAR SERIES temporary street circuits, with a variety of surfaces, including asphalt and concrete, and many bumps.

The test comes after three days of laps by Rossi and Palou in early August on the IMS road course for the car’s on-track debut, followed by the car’s oval debut in testing in early September at IMS.

Also turning laps those two days will be Kyle Kirkwood of Andretti Global and Scott McLaughlin of Team Penske, testing tires for Firestone in current NTT INDYCAR SERIES machinery.

White House Congratulates CGR for Title

Team owner Chip Ganassi received a letter from President Donald J. Trump congratulating him and his Chip Ganassi Racing team for Alex Palou’s fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship this season, the record-setting 18th INDYCAR SERIES title for the organization.

“Chip Ganassi Racing continues to be at the forefront of the racing world,” Trump wrote. “Your team is composed of elite competitors who consistently demonstrate grit, hard work, and dedication.”

Trump, his wife, Melania, and other Cabinet and government officials were honored guests during the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. on Aug. 23 on the streets of the nation’s capital.

title: 1 day ago •Team News Team Penske To Continue Long Partnership With Chevrolet
excerpt:
1 day ago

Team Penske and Chevrolet announced Oct. 8 a multiyear extension of their partnership that will keep the most successful team in NTT INDYCAR SERIES history with the manufacturer that has powered much of that success.

That heritage of winning includes nine victories in the Indianapolis 500 with drivers Rick Mears, Emerson Fittipaldi, Helio Castroneves, Juan Pablo Montoya, Will Power, Simon Pagenaud and Josef Newgarden.

“Chevrolet has been a terrific partner for our NTT INDYCAR SERIES team, both on and off the track,” Roger Penske said. “While winning on the track is certainly important, Team Penske’s partnership with Chevrolet extends far beyond that. We are excited that this extension will take us well into the future as we work to build on the success we have enjoyed together in the INDYCAR SERIES.”

The 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season saw Team Penske and Chevrolet open the year with the pole position on the streets of St. Petersburg while capping the campaign with a win at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. For the season, Team Penske added to the Chevrolet victory ledger with wins at Phoenix Raceway, World Wide Technology Raceway and Laguna Seca, respectively, along with earning three pole positions in 2026.

Since officially joining forces for the 1986 INDYCAR SERIES season with a manufacturer-backed relationship, Team Penske and Chevrolet have visited Victory Lane 125 times and have captured 157 pole positions, including Scott McLaughlin’s NTT P1 Award in September at Laguna Seca that represented Chevrolet’s 250th INDYCAR SERIES pole position.

Team Penske first began competing in INDYCAR with legendary driver Mark Donohue driving a Chevrolet-powered Eagle in the USAC-sanctioned race June 15, 1968, at Canadian Tire Motorsports Park.

“For decades, Team Penske and Chevrolet have had one of the strongest competitive relationships in all of motorsport, built on a foundation of trust, a shared commitment to technical excellence, and a relentless focus on winning,” General Motors President Mark Reuss said. “The results of our partnership speak for themselves, but we’re also driven by what comes next. This extension ensures our teams remain aligned and steadfast in our pursuit of more poles, more wins and more Indy 500 victories together.”

This was the third extension agreement between Chevrolet and an INDYCAR SERIES team announced this week, with Penske’s pact joining those signed with Arrow McLaren and ECR.

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season starts Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line: Top Ganassi Championship Season?
excerpt:
Today’s question: Chip Ganassi Racing won its record-setting 18th NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship this year. What’s one of those championship seasons you’d like to highlight?

Curt Cavin: The 1996 season was embroiled in the politics of a divided sport, so many of the accomplishments of the drivers and their teams didn’t get the credit they deserved. Among those was Jimmy Vasser, who became Chip Ganassi Racing’s first season championship in ‘96. That year, Jimmy (photo, above, center) won three of Champ Car’s first four races and then won the highly anticipated U.S. 500, the Memorial Day weekend race at Michigan International Speedway that countered the Indy Racing League’s Indianapolis 500. Jimmy finished the season 22 points ahead of Michael Andretti and Alex Zanardi while besting a field that included eight drivers who earned series championships in their careers. Because of the split, Jimmy didn’t participate at Indy for four of his best years in the sport, so his talent isn’t as regarded as it should have been. Jimmy had two other top-three series finishes (third in ’97, second in ’98), and he won eight poles and 10 races amid that highly competitive late-1990s.

Eric Smith: It’s 2009 for me. Dario Franchitti rejoined the INDYCAR SERIES following a disappointing year in NASCAR. He won the 2007 INDYCAR SERIES title with Andretti Autosport, left to join CGR in NASCAR, then returned to open-wheel racing in 2009 and won a narrow championship by 11 points over teammate Scott Dixon. Franchitti won the season finale while Dixon tried to stretch his fuel strategy but had to pit with eight laps to go at Homestead. He finished third in the race but second in the championship, one of three times the team finished 1-2 occurred joining 1998 and 2023. Franchitti (photo, top, right) and Dixon (photo, top, left) combined to win 10 of the 17 races that year, tying 1998 for the most wins by a team in a single season. Franchitti had 15 top-10 finishes, while Dixon had 14.

Arni Sribhen: Dario Franchitti thought he was done with INDYCAR SERIES racing after winning both the Indianapolis 500 and NTT INDYCAR SERIES title in 2007. But after a brief and aborted foray into NASCAR with Chip Ganassi Racing in 2008, Ganassi put Franchitti back in an INDYCAR SERIES car for 2009. And what a comeback season it was. Franchitti won five races, including a masterclass in fuel saving at Homestead, to steal the title from reigning champion Scott Dixon and Team Penske’s Ryan Briscoe. It was the first of three straight title wins for Franchitti and paired with two Indy 500 wins over the next four seasons, lifted him into the status of one of this generation’s greats.

Paul Kelly: It’s absolutely 2009 for me, too, for so many reasons – some also listed above. Dario Franchitti and Scott Dixon finished 1-2 in the standings and won 10 of 17 races. This wasn’t the first time Chip Ganassi Racing drivers finished 1-2 in the standings – Alex Zanardi and Jimmy Vasser first achieved the feat in 1998 for the team. And it wasn’t the last, as Alex Palou and Dixon were 1-2 in 2023. But I elevate 2009 over those other two seasons for two reasons. One, Franchitti and Dixon were the team’s only drivers in 2009, yet they still finished 1-2. Team Penske drivers have finished 1-2 in the standings five times since 2014, an incredible achievement. But those were three- or four-driver teams, so Penske could have a driver or two with a down year and still have a shot at finishing 1-2. Two, Franchitti and Dixon were so competitive with each other in 2009. Franchitti finished just 11 points ahead of his teammate. In 1998, Zanardi was 116 points ahead of Vasser, and Palou beat Dixon by 78 in 2023. The 2009 race featured true competition between two all-time greats of the sport. It was fantastic.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Team News ECR, Chevrolet Agree to Multiyear Partnership Extension
excerpt:
ECR and Chevrolet announced Oct. 7 a multiyear extension of their longstanding partnership.

Indianapolis-based ECR is one of only two teams to have been powered by Chevrolet since the introduction of the 2.2-liter twin-turbo V6. During the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, ECR will reach its 500th race start, continuing a relationship with Chevrolet that dates back to the team’s inception in 2012.

The extension comes as the NTT INDYCAR SERIES prepares to introduce a new chassis and engine formula in 2028. Alexander Rossi, driver of ECR’s No. 20 Java House Chevrolet, is one of two drivers to have participated in the first tests of the series’ new chassis. As development progresses, ECR will have the opportunity to be involved in testing Chevrolet’s new powerplant.

“Chevrolet has been with ECR since the beginning of our team, and they have been an important part of our team’s growth over our first 15 seasons,” ECR co-owner and CEO Ed Carpenter said. “We’ve had a lot of success with Chevy over the years, and we’re proud to be one of only two teams to have partnered with Chevrolet since its return to INDYCAR. Maintaining that continuity is very important to us as we not only approach our 500th race start but also enter the next era of INDYCAR competition.

“We’re very proud of our history with Chevrolet and are looking forward to adding to it.”

ECR and Chevrolet have won nine races and six NTT P1 Awards together, including three poles by Carpenter for the Indianapolis 500.

“ECR has been an important part of Chevrolet’s INDYCAR program, and this extension reflects the strength of the technical relationship we’ve built together,” said Eric Warren, General Motors vice president of global motorsports competition. “As the series moves toward its next-generation car and powertrain, close collaboration between our engineers will be critical. We share a clear objective with ECR: to keep raising the performance of the Chevrolet package and compete for wins, championships and Indianapolis 500 victories.”

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season begins Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: Arrow McLaren Staying With Chevrolet Power for Multiple Seasons
excerpt:
Arrow McLaren announced Oct. 6 a multiyear extension with Chevrolet as its engine manufacturer, reaffirming the organizations’ longstanding technical partnership as the NTT INDYCAR SERIES prepares for its next era of innovation.

The extension comes at a pivotal moment for both Arrow McLaren and Chevrolet as the series completes early testing phases for the new Dallara IR-28 chassis set to debut in 2028 competition. The next generation platform will introduce improved aerodynamic architecture, an upgraded power-to-weight ratio, new wing packages designed for better racing and overall improved safety systems — all areas where early manufacturer involvement is essential.

"Our extension with Chevrolet is key to our overall goal of winning both the INDYCAR championship and the Indy 500,” McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown said. “Over the past seven seasons, the team and Chevy have been working closely together through various developments, and the work now ahead of us with the 2028 chassis will be critical in determining our competitiveness. Mark Reuss, Eric Warren, Jim Campbell and everyone across the Chevy and GM organization are committed to executing at the highest level and share our absolute focus on winning. I’m excited for what’s to come with this strengthened relationship."

Since McLaren Racing entered the series full time in 2020 with Schmidt Peterson Motorsports to become Arrow McLaren SP, the Arrow McLaren and Chevrolet collaboration has achieved 14 Chevy-powered wins, 54 podiums and 13 NTT P1 Awards. Chevy also secured three consecutive Manufacturers’ Championships from 2022-24.

“Arrow McLaren has been an important part of Chevrolet’s INDYCAR program, and this extension reflects the strength of the technical relationship we’ve built together,” said Eric Warren, General Motors vice president of global motorsports competition. “As the series moves toward the next generation of car and powertrain development, close collaboration between our engineers will be critical. We continue to share a clear objective with Arrow McLaren: to keep raising the performance of the Chevrolet package and compete for wins, championships and the Indianapolis 500."

Team veteran Pato O’Ward welcomes six-time series champion Scott Dixon and 2026 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Felix Rosenqvist to the team’s three-driver lineup starting in 2027.

title: Friendly Rivalry Reaches Top Level for Kyle Kirkwood, David Malukas
excerpt:
Kyle Kirkwood and David Malukas have followed remarkably similar paths to the top of the sport.

They raced each other in Florida karting events as kids, battled for an INDY NXT championship and now compete for two of the most successful teams in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. Their careers have taken different turns, but the longtime friendly rivals share a common goal: catching Alex Palou.

Palou, who turned 29 on April 1, has won five championships in six NTT INDYCAR SERIES seasons with Chip Ganassi Racing. His four consecutive titles from 2023-26 tie Sébastien Bourdais’ 2004-07 run for the longest championship streak in series history.

Kirkwood, who turns 28 on Oct. 19, is from Jupiter, Florida, and drives for Andretti Global. Malukas, who turned 25 on Sept. 27, is from Chicago and races for Team Penske. Both believe they can be among the drivers capable of challenging Palou’s dominance.

“It’s crazy to see how far we’ve come,” Malukas said. “Now he’s (Kirkwood) with Andretti. I’m at Penske, and that battle still continues. So, it’s cool to see us as a generation make it all the way to the top.”

Their rivalry began long before either reached the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. Kirkwood and Malukas started racing karts in Florida in 2009. They continued competing against each other through the junior ranks before emerging as the two dominant drivers of the 2021 INDY NXT season. Kirkwood won the championship by 13 points over Malukas, with the pair combining to win 17 of the season’s 20 races (photo, above. Credit: Gavin Baker Photography).

Their paths eventually led to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, where both were part of the 2022 rookie class. Kirkwood drove for AJ Foyt Racing, while Malukas joined Dale Coyne Racing.

Kirkwood moved to Andretti Global for the 2023 season and quickly established himself as a race winner, earning his first series victory in the prestigious Acura Grand Prix of Long Beach, the third event of the season. He added another win later that year on the streets of Nashville.

Malukas’ progression took a more complicated route. After two seasons with Dale Coyne Racing, he was scheduled to join Arrow McLaren in 2024. But an offseason mountain biking accident left him injured and unable to compete. The team released him before he made a start.

Malukas returned to competition with Meyer Shank Racing for the final 10 races of the 2024 season before spending 2025 with Foyt’s team. Then came his biggest opportunity yet. Team Penske signed Malukas for the 2026 season, giving him the chance to drive for one of the most successful organizations in INDYCAR SERIES history.

It also put two drivers who had competed against each other since childhood in positions they once could only have imagined. Kirkwood was established at Andretti Global. Malukas was now wearing Team Penske colors. Their careers had taken different turns, but the friendly rivalry remained.

“We’ve been through it all,” Malukas said of Kirkwood. “We went through different ranks. We went through feeder series. We’ve been racing each other since I was picking my nose, playing with Hot Wheels, go-karting. The Florida Winter Tour -- that’s where the battle all started.”

This isn’t the first time for a connection like this. Tony Kanaan and Helio Castroneves took a similar path from competing as kids in Brazil to junior open-wheel categories in the United States to the INDYCAR SERIES. The same type of friendly rivalry existed through junior categories for Pato O’Ward and Colton Herta, especially in their fierce race for the INDY NXT title in 2018.

Kirkwood sees the same connection. So much so, he ran into Malukas’ father, Henry, before he climbed into his car in the season finale at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. Kirkwood said he and Malukas’ dad reflected on how far the two drivers had come.

“I said it’s cool if you look back at when we were in karting together,” Kirkwood said. “We were on the same team in karting many years ago. It’s pretty cool to look and be like, ‘Hey, we’re fighting for positions in a championship, pretty high positions in a championship in INDYCAR.’”

Kirkwood finished second in points in the 2026 season while Malukas was fifth, the top Team Penske points finisher. Kirkwood is well aware what makes Malukas such a formidable opponent, one he believes will earn his first series win sooner than later.

“He’s a phenomenal driver,” Kirkwood said. “He definitely does the things that I do poorly extremely well. I’ve learned a lot racing against him over the years.”

That familiarity could become an advantage as both drivers continue their pursuit of Palou. They know each other’s strengths. They have watched each other develop. And they have competed against each other every step of the way. Now, they have the equipment and experience to contend at the front of the championship.

“I’m proud to be part of the era he’s in because he’s an exceptional driver,” Kirkwood said. “I think for many years to come, he’s going to be someone knocking on the door of a championship.”

title: Surprise, Surprise: Biggest 2026 Stunners in NTT INDYCAR SERIES
excerpt:
Sports seasons regularly produce surprises, which is part of what makes them endearing. The NTT INDYCAR SERIES certainly had its share of surprises in 2026.

Of course, Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou winning a fourth consecutive season championship and fifth in six years wasn’t one of them. And a second consecutive sellout of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge, which occurred in May, was largely expected given the momentum the event and the sport have built in recent years.

It also wasn’t much of a surprise that television viewership of races took another large gain – a 23 percent year-over-year increase – given the investment and commitment FOX has made in the sport. But there were plenty of things that caught people off guard this year. A look at them somewhat sequentially.

INDYCAR Having a Street Race Where?!

There had only been whispers of a new street race in the nation’s capital, but it seemed like a dream that couldn’t come true. So, the news was a shocker when it was announced Jan. 30.

Along with the “500,” the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. on Aug. 23 became a signature moment of the season, the kind of event that almost seemed incomprehensible given the hurdles that needed to be overcome and the city’s magnificent backdrops.

Television ratings were through the roof: 3.28 million people tuned in, making it the most-watched race other than Indy since 1995.

The Washington race (photo, above) was one of three new street races in 2026, and each contributed to the success of the season. With the support of the Dallas Cowboys and the Texas Rangers, the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington will be keeper along with the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham, a relocation of the Toronto street race.

Andretti Global drivers captured all three events, with Kyle Kirkwood winning in Arlington and Washington and Marcus Ericsson victorious in Markham.

Schumacher (Yes, That Schumacher!) Shines on Ovals

The series’ return to Phoenix Raceway for the first time since 2018 went very well, and one of the standouts made his oval-track debut.

Mick Schumacher is best known for being the only son of seven-time Formula One champion Michael Schumacher, who often made it clear he didn’t want any part of INDYCAR’s high-speed oval thrillers. But Mick (photo, above) adapted just fine, so much so that his best performances in the first year in this series were on oval tracks.

Driving Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing’s No. 47 Honda, Schumacher was quick straight away at Phoenix, qualifying in the fourth position. In the race, he remained on the lead lap until his crew struggled with a tire change on the pit stop at Lap 71. That bobble dropped Schumacher to the 21st position; he finished the race in 18th place.

That was a preview of oval success to come for the Swiss-born German driver. Schumacher completed all 200 laps in the “500,” finishing a respectable 18th to earn Rookie of the Year honors. He backed up that performance by finishing 16th in the Bommarito Automotive Group 500 at World Wide Technology Raceway, was eighth in the Borchetta Bourbon Music City Grand Prix at Nashville Superspeedway and earned the 13th- and 12th-place finishes in the Snap-on INDYCAR Weekend, a doubleheader at the tricky Milwaukee Mile.

Schumacher finished second to Dale Coyne Racing’s Dennis Hauger for the series’ Rookie of the Year Award. AJ Foyt Racing’s Caio Collet finished third.

Rosenqvist Wins Indy in a Thriller

Felix Rosenqvist certainly had been competitive in past oval races at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, finishing fourth in 2022 and 2025. But he’d never had a final lap like he delivered in this year’s race – in fact, no one had.

Rosenqvist, who had started fourth and led 24 laps, began Lap 200 in the third position. He got a terrific run coming to the white flag and drew alongside Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian teammate Marcus Armstrong as they crossed the historic Yard of Bricks.

Winning Indy is never easy, and this one certainly wasn’t for the Swede. He spent most of the lap driving on the outside of Armstrong before finally clearing him in the middle of Turn 4. From there it seemed like Rosenqvist’s car was shot out of a cannon as he quickly closed on race leader David Malukas of Team Penske, sweeping past him just ahead of the checkered flag. The separation was a scant .0233 of a second (photo, above), the closest 1-2 finish in the history of “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.” The previous record was .043 of a second in 1992.

The breathtaking race featured an event-record 70 lead changes, breaking the previous mark of 68 set in 2013. With his second career NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory, Rosenqvist became the third Swedish driver to win Indy, joining Kenny Brack (1999) and Ericsson (2022). Meyer Shank Racing won the “500” for a second time, the other being Helio Castroneves’ record-tying fourth victory in 2021.

Dixon’s Switch Biggest of Silly Season

After 25 seasons and six NTT INDYCAR SERIES championships, Scott Dixon made the startling switch of employers, leaving Chip Ganassi Racing for Arrow McLaren.

Dixon (photo, top) had won 58 races and six series championships with Chip Ganassi’s organization, the partnership becoming an all-time standard in the sport. Dixon joined the team in 2002 and ended his time there after 414 starts, including a series-record 374 consecutively.

Joining Dixon on the move was Rosenqvist, who became the first reigning “500” champion since 2017 winner Takuma Sato to switch teams for the next season. Dixon and Rosenqvist will join Pato O’Ward and Ryan Hunter-Reay for the team’s stellar cast at Indy.

CGR filled Dixon’s seat with Christian Lundgaard, whom Arrow McLaren chose not to re-sign after winning two races and finishing third in the final point standings. MSR elevated Armstrong, who finished fifth at Indy, and added Schumacher for next season.

Schumacher’s former team – Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing – announced it will be a two-car operation in 2027. Dreyer & Reinbold Racing will join the series full-time with Conor Daly as its Honda driver after purchasing a charter from RLL. Several other seats for next year’s lineup are still to be determined.

VeeKay, Juncos Hollinger Racing Earn Top-10 Standing

Rinus VeeKay and Juncos Hollinger Racing took a bite out of many of the sport’s big dogs by finishing 10th in the standings, the highest career finish for both the driver and the team.

VeeKay (photo, above) had finished 12th in two previous seasons – in 2021 and 2023 – while JHR’s prior best was 16th in 2023 with Callum Ilott at the wheel.

This pairing finished third in the second race of the Snap-on INDYCAR Weekend doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile and added three fourth-place finishes. Somewhat overlooked was another outstanding performance: sixth in the “500,” a best finish for the driver and the team.

title: INDYCAR Drivers Extending Seasons at Petit Le Mans IMSA Finale
excerpt:
Drivers from the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT by Firestone are extending their racing seasons by competing in all four classes of Motul Petit Le Mans, the season-ending IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Oct. 1-3 at Road Atlanta.

INDYCAR SERIES champions Scott Dixon and Alex Palou will be teammates – perhaps for the last time after their six seasons together at Chip Ganassi Racing – in the premier Grand Touring Prototype (GTP) class in the 10-hour race Saturday, sharing separate entries for Acura Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian.

Six-time series champion Dixon will share the No. 60 Acura ARX-06 with former INDYCAR SERIES drivers Tom Blomqvist and Colin Braun on the 12-turn, 2.54-mile road course in Braselton, Georgia. Dixon is leaving Chip Ganassi Racing at the end of this year after 24 full-time seasons to join Arrow McLaren next season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

Five-time series champion Palou will start two consecutive weekends of sports car racing by sharing the No. 93 Acura ARX-06 (photo, top; courtesy IMSA Photo) with Nick Yelloly and Renger van der Zande. Palou also is driving in the Indianapolis 8 Hour Intercontinental GT Challenge race Oct. 10 on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course.

Palou and Dixon have a good chance at overall victory Saturday if speed in the opening practice Thursday is any indication. Yelloly was quickest at 1 minute, 11.506 seconds in the No. 93, while Braun was a whisker slower at 1:11.509 in the No. 60.

Not only is this event an end to Dixon and Palou as teammates, but it also marks the end of Acura’s prototype program in IMSA and with MSR.

In another note of interest in the GTP class, former INDYCAR SERIES driver Colton Herta is returning to America to share the No. 40 Cadillac Wayne Taylor Racing Cadillac V-Series.R with Jordan Taylor and Louis Deletraz. Herta had a disappointing first season in 2026 in Formula 2, the final step on the ladder to Formula One.

The GT Daytona PRO (GTD PRO) class features two INDY NXT by Firestone champions among its driver lineups.

2021 INDY NXT champion and 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES runner-up Kyle Kirkwood will return to the No. 14 Vasser Sullivan Racing Lexus RC F GT3 as a teammate to former INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT driver Jack Hawksworth and Ben Barnicoat. Kirkwood was quickest in the class in practice Thursday.

Freshly crowned INDY NXT champion Nikita Johnson will race in the No. 59 RLL Team McLaren McLaren 720S EVO GT3 (photo, above) that he also drove in the TireRack.com Battle on the Bricks on Sept. 20 at IMS.

The Le Mans Prototype 2 (LMP2) and GT Daytona (GTD) classes each feature one active INDY NXT by Firestone driver.

Jacob Abel is sharing the No. 18 Era Motorsport LMP2 car, while James Roe is in the driver lineup for the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG GT3 in GTD.

Live coverage of the 10-hour race begins from noon-3 p.m. ET Saturday on NBC, followed by 3-10:30 p.m. ET on NBCSN. The entire race also will be streamed on Peacock.

title: Christian Lundgaard was the 'obvious' choice to replace Scott Dixon at Chip Ganassi Racing
excerpt:
Arguably the worst kept secret in racing over the past couple months was that Christian Lundgaard was taking over the vacant seat at Chip Ganassi Racing left by Scott Dixon.

Dixon, a six-time IndyCar champion, essentially completed a swap between CGR and Arrow-McLaren, moving to McLaren after 24 seasons at Ganassi.

Lundgaard was officially announced as the driver of the No. 9 Honda for 2027 on Tuesday.

Lundgaard will join 21-year-old Kyffin Simpson and five-time IndyCar champion Alex Palou at Ganassi. Lundgaard is coming off a career year in 2026 that saw him win two races and finish third in the IndyCar standings.

"I think the first thought that I had when this came on the table and became an opportunity was, I am learning from the best driver who learned from the best driver in Scott Dixon," Lundgaard said on a media call Tuesday, "And I think just getting to learn as much as I can from there. And obviously joining CGR and Chip and the 18 championships, it's really just a dream come true in many ways.

"It's one of those opportunities you never expected to rise, and I'm just super excited to join Chip Ganassi and PNC Bank."

With Palou and Lundgaard racing together as teammates, CGR will have arguably the best duo in all of IndyCar racing next season.

Why Chip Ganassi wanted Christian Lundgaard

"Obviously we looked at everybody," Ganassi said. "You look at everybody that's available. I mean, yeah, we obviously looked at everybody that was out there and available... But Christian's name kept landing back as the obvious one. Like wait a minute, we're not overlooking this guy, are we?

"Every name that came along, we said, okay, well, how does that compare with Lundgaard, whether it's somebody who hasn't been in the series, and did they have to learn the tracks, and are they current with this type of drive style that you need, or are they committed to maybe coming to the U.S."

Of course, Lundgaard won't be filling the shoes of any driver. Dixon won 58 races, six titles and 32 poles while driving for CGR. While he struggled to find pace in 2026, his legacy with the team is giant and unshakeable.

Those numbers will inevitably put Lundgaard under a microscope throughout his tenure with the organization.

"We just look for people with talent," Ganassi said. "I think everything else can sort of be taught. You saw at the end of last season at Milwaukee, he was obviously doing very well on ovals. I think it all has to do with his prerequisites — before being at Ganassi, his prerequisites, he's taken something away from all of those to develop into the driver that he is today. So he has five years of experience in the series. He's been to the Indianapolis 500 now a handful of times.

"These are all things that are no small thing when you're coming into a new environment that make you attractive to a new team. And he seems to be able to keep the car on the — he keeps the rubber side down and the shiny side up, as they say. He keeps the car on the track, so that develops into points. And as you know, we like those guys that can amass points."

Time will tell if Lundgaard can build a comparable legacy to Dixon, but it'd be surprising if he's not immediately in contention for race wins and championships at CGR beginning next season.

Quotes provided by IndyCar Media.

title: Christian Lundgaard Sees Opportunity, Not Pressure, in Ganassi Ride
excerpt:
Christian Lundgaard isn’t feeling the pressure. That’s not to say he doesn’t understand what awaits him in 2027.

The 25-year-old Dane (photo, top), who finished third in points in the 2026 season with Arrow McLaren, takes over the No. 9 PNC Bank Honda at Chip Ganassi Racing. He replaces Scott Dixon, who spent 24 full-time seasons with the organization, won six championships, 58 of his 59 career victories and the 2008 Indianapolis 500.

That is a difficult history to follow. But each side views this as a perfect opportunity.

“I’m super excited,” team owner Chip Ganassi said. “When’s the last time the guy that’s finished third in the points was available? That says it all to me.”

Lundgaard was Arrow McLaren’s highest point scorer in 2026 and won twice, giving him two victories, 13 podium finishes and 14 top-five results in his two seasons with the team.

Yet in early July, Lundgaard learned Arrow McLaren would not offer him a contract for 2027. Suddenly, a driver who at the time was also third in the championship was looking for a new home. He was disappointed and confused.

“I found out a couple of hours before the media found out,” Lundgaard said. “I sort of had an idea that was a possibility. I tried to just keep my head down.”

The timing was significant. Part of the Lundgaard announcement was that the team had signed Dixon to join Pato O’Ward for 2027, with Felix Rosenqvist also joining the organization. That left Ganassi looking for a replacement for one of the most accomplished drivers in team history. Lundgaard emerged as a logical fit.

But a fit like that creates expectations. Lundgaard is aware he cannot simply step into the No. 9 Honda (photo, above) and replicate what Dixon accomplished. In the same breath, he also knows he is joining an organization that has repeatedly turned talented drivers into champions.

Dixon won the championship in his first full-time season with Ganassi in 2003. Juan Montoya did the same in 1999, Dario Franchitti in 2009 and Alex Palou in 2021, the first of five titles in six years, including the last four.

“The first thought that I had when this opportunity became on the table was, I’m learning from the best driver (Alex Palou), who learned from the best driver in Scott Dixon,” Lundgaard said. “Getting to learn as much as I can from there. It really is just a dream come true in many ways. It’s one of those opportunities you never expected to rise.”

But there is one question Lundgaard must answer – performance on ovals. That was one of the reasons cited for Arrow McLaren’s decision to drop him. Ganassi doesn’t see the same limitation. He sees an area where Lundgaard can continue to develop and one of the reasons he believed he was “best available” for hire.

“I like his approach to driving,” Ganassi said. “I think he’s very clinical. I think he’s a student of the craft. I didn’t see any oval questions at Milwaukee. That’s an oval. He beat all three of our guys. I’m not concerned.”

The Milwaukee Mile doubleheader in August was significant for Lundgaard. He finished third, earning his first top-five finish on a circle track, during the final oval race of the 2026 season. He finished sixth in the other race of the doubleheader. That was another indication that Lundgaard’s oval results are trending in the right direction.

His average oval finish has improved in each of his first five seasons in the series, from 18.4 as a rookie to 17.6, 15.3, 13.2 and 10.8. Ganassi believes there is more to come.

“In some of our first meetings, I grilled him (Lundgaard) pretty extensively on what we expect,” Ganassi said. “We have a great culture. I’m confident that our system will continue to develop Christian in the same manner.

“You look at Christian’s age and his experience in the series. He’s learned the circuits. He understands the paddock. We look for people with talent. Everything else can sort of be taught.”

Lundgaard admitted joining Ganassi is a tough situation to enter. He’s replacing a six-time champion and joining a five-time champion.

“We know the cars are fast,” Lundgaard said. “That’s the thing I need to keep in mind. I need to learn as much as possible and do the simple things right. That’s something CGR has been very good at.

“I know what I’m capable of and why I’ve been hired. Trying to learn as much as possible and get the most out of it. The main objective is to get a CGR car to Victory Lane.”

Ganassi said: “He seems to be able to keep the rubber side down and shiny side up, as they say. Those drivers keep the car on the track, and that turns into points.”

That’s why Lundgaard believes this is the right opportunity to take him to the next level. Take what Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing taught, McLaren believed was missing from his game and combine it with what Ganassi already sees in him to find out what the next chapter can produce.

“We’re in the business to win but also create some great stories,” Lundgaard said.

title: INDYCAR Notebook: Foyt Renews With Longtime Partner
excerpt:
AJ Foyt Racing announced Sept. 30 a multiyear agreement with Hendricks Holding Company, Inc., the Beloit, Wisconsin-based private investment firm whose portfolio includes ABC Supply Co., Inc., Hendricks Commercial Properties, Geronimo Hospitality Group and other manufacturing, construction and transportation companies.

The agreement extends a relationship that began with ABC Supply in 2005 and will continue the Hendricks family's support of the No. 14 Homes For Our Troops Chevrolet (photo, top) and its national platform for America's severely injured post-9/11 veterans.

Since the 2022 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge, the Hendricks family and its companies have used AJ Foyt Racing entries to spotlight Homes For Our Troops (HFOT), whose mission is to build and donate mortgage-free, specially adapted custom homes to severely injured post-9/11 veterans. The effort began when ABC Supply donated the design of the No. 11 Chevrolet to HFOT for the 2022 Indianapolis 500 and paired the program with a matching-donation campaign.

The partnership expanded in 2026 to a full-season No. 14 Homes For Our Troops Chevrolet, supported by Hendricks Commercial Properties and Geronimo Hospitality Group, giving HFOT a national platform throughout the NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

Since its inception in 2004, Homes For Our Troops has built and donated 445 homes in 46 states and has 66 projects underway. HFOT homes feature more than 40 major special adaptations, including wider halls and doorways, automatic door openers, roll-under sinks, stovetops and counters, pull-down shelving, roll-in showers, backup generators and safe rooms. These adaptations are designed to enable veterans to live more independently and focus on family, recovery and future opportunities.

The No. 14 Homes For Our Troops Chevrolet will be driven in 2027 by Dennis Hauger, the 23-year-old Norwegian who earned 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year honors. Hauger, the 2025 INDY NXT by Firestone champion, has raced in the United States since 2025 and joins AJ Foyt Racing on a multiyear agreement.

Palou, Ericsson To Race in Indianapolis 8 Hour Next Weekend

Five-time and reigning NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou and fellow Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Marcus Ericsson will compete in sports car racing by driving in the Indianapolis 8 Hour race Oct. 9-11 on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course.

2025 Indianapolis 500 winner Palou (photo, above) joins title hopeful Luca Stolz and AMG Junior Lin Hodenius in the No. 80 Lone Star Racing Mercedes-AMG in the Intercontinental GT Challenge event on the 14-turn, 2.439-mile road course. Palou drove in the event with Lone Star in 2024, finishing 13th after his co-drivers’ stints were plagued by electrical problems.

“The Indianapolis Motor Speedway is a special place for me, and I am excited to be returning for another shot at the Indianapolis 8 Hour with Mercedes-AMG Team Lone Star Racing,” Palou said. “I have some unfinished business from my 2024 GT3 outing, so I am really happy to reunite with the team to have another opportunity to aim for the race win.

“I always love the atmosphere and the fans there, and I look forward to having an exciting race to finish the 2026 season with hopefully another memorable trophy.”

2022 Indianapolis 500 winner Ericsson will join his younger brother, Hampus Ericsson, and Derek DeBoer in the Random Vandals Racing BMW M4 GT3 EVO. The team will compete in the Pro-Am class entry for the GT World Challenge America powered by AWS and Intercontinental GT Challenge season finale.

Marcus Ericsson has previous GT3 experience, including driving in this year’s Rolex 24 At Daytona in a Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2 fielded by Wayne Taylor Racing. The Ericsson brothers teamed up for the first time in a Leiper Motorsport Lamborghini in the Michelin 12 Hour Malaysia race last December at Sepang International Circuit.

“I’m incredibly excited to join Derek and my younger brother Hampus in the Random Vandals Racing No. 99 BMW,” Ericsson said. “Racing alongside Hampus and sharing a car with him is something I cherish deeply, so I’m very grateful to Random Vandals for giving us the opportunity to do this together.

Visit IMS.com to buy tickets or for more information about the Indianapolis 8 Hour.

St. Petersburg Ticket Renewal Period Starts Thursday

The exclusive renewal period begins at 10 a.m. ET Thursday, Oct. 1 for the 2027 Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg. Fans who purchased 3-Day Grandstand tickets to the 2026 race weekend are eligible and will have until Monday, Oct. 19 to renew their same seats for the 2027 event. Public ticket sales will begin on Friday, Oct. 23.

The 23rd edition of the iconic downtown St. Petersburg waterfront event is set for March 5-7 and will be headlined by the NTT INDYCAR SERIES once again Sunday.

The Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg features Gold, Silver, and Bronze Grandstand seating designations for 2027. Renewal customers purchasing 3-Day Grandstand seats will receive complimentary Firestone IndyCar Paddock Passes, which allow fans to get close to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES cars and drivers during the race weekend.

Renewals will be available online at gpstpete.com with pricing starting at $150 for reserved 3-Day Grandstand seats. For all ticket pricing and 2027 event information, visit gpstpete.com.

title: Inside Line: Most Interesting 2027 Open Seat or Silly Season Driver?
excerpt:
Today’s question: Christian Lundgaard was named Sept. 29 to drive the No. 9 Chip Ganassi Racing Honda in a multiyear deal, one of the most coveted of the open seats for next season. Which remaining open seat for the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season or driver in contention for those seats interests you the most?

Curt Cavin: I think it’s a sure thing, but we still need to have Rinus VeeKay confirmed at Juncos Hollinger Racing. That pairing was one of the best of the 2026 season, earning a third-place finish at the Milwaukee Mile and netting three fourth-place finishes and a sixth-place finish in the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge en route to a 10th-place standings finish. The best guess here is the announcement will come once team ownership details are finalized, but VeeKay (photo, above) will be back in the seat, and the sport will be better for it.

Eric Smith: I’m intrigued by the second seat at AJ Foyt Racing. It’s no secret Josh Pierson has the inside line (no pun intended) for the ride, but that’s also predicated on a looming evaluation test. What if it doesn’t go well? Santino Ferrucci lacks the budget, or he’d likely be in one of the cars. So, who ends up in this seat if it’s not Pierson (photo, above)? The Foyt cars have shown promise lately, particularly at Indianapolis Motor Speedway. The team is also going to garner plenty of attention next May, with it being the 60th anniversary of A.J. Foyt’s third Indy 500 victory and the 50th anniversary of his becoming the first driver to win the “500” four times. This open seat has my eyes and what the eventual driver can bring since the other seat is vacated by this past season’s Rookie of the Year, Dennis Hauger. There’s a potential that neither Foyt driver brings much NTT INDYCAR SERIES experience to 2027.

Arni Sribhen: The open NTT INDYCAR SERIES seat that intrigues me the most is the one that may go to an 18-year-old kid. I’m talking about reigning INDY NXT by Firestone champion Nikita Johnson (photo, top), who lit up the developmental series in 2026 and is probably sitting on his boat in the Gulf of Mexico, ignoring his phone as it blows up. AJ Foyt Racing, Dale Coyne Racing and Juncos Hollinger Racing have all knocked on the door trying to lock down this Floridian phenom for a full-time seat. Here’s the open secret in the paddock right now: Johnson already knows exactly which fire suit he wants to wear next season, but the newcomer may not get to pick his place when budget comes into play. Still, whichever team gets the youngster will get a talented rookie with a veteran’s racing IQ. He knows how to keep his nose clean and squeeze every drop of potential out of his car. He could be the next big thing in INDYCAR, and the teams that don’t get him now may regret it later.

Paul Kelly: I’m wondering if this is the end of the line for Romain Grosjean in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. He arrived in the series in 2021 at the peak of his fame after cheating death in a fiery crash in the last drive of his Formula One career in 2020 at Bahrain. Most assumed he might be a title contender and would win races, especially when driving for Andretti Global in 2022 and 2023, but that didn’t happen. Grosjean (photo, above) endured an uninspiring season in 2026 with his return to the series with Dale Coyne Racing after a one-year hiatus. The big highlight was an impressive second at Markham, but that was one of just three top-10 finishes. Team owner Coyne may want to keep a veteran to mentor a rookie, perhaps INDY NXT by Firestone champion Nikita Johnson, after the unexpected departure of Dennis Hauger to AJ Foyt Racing for 2027. But Callum Ilott and Nolan Siegel also are on the market, too, and almost certainly would require a smaller pay packet than Grosjean. And maybe Grosjean has had enough of running mid-pack or deeper in the INDYCAR SERIES and wants to head back to sports cars. Interesting times ahead, but we may have seen the last of “The Phoenix” in INDYCAR.

title: Independent Officiating Board Members Extended for 2027
excerpt:
Managing Director of Officiating Elkins Also Confirmed for 2027

INDYCAR has announced extensions for Independent Officiating Board (IOB) members Ray Evernham, Raj Nair and Ronan Morgan for the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT by Firestone seasons.

This month, INDYCAR’s charter team owners unanimously agreed to retain Evernham and Nair, and the Federation Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) reappointed Morgan as the series looks to the second year of INDYCAR Officiating.

Nair is a 30-year veteran of the automotive and auto racing industries with vast experience and technical compliance expertise as an executive at Singer Group, Inc., Multimatic, Inc. and Ford Motor Company. He served as the IOB’s chair during the 2026 INDYCAR season.

Evernham is a longtime motorsports veteran who most notably served as the crew chief for three of Jeff Gordon’s NASCAR Cup Series championships before he pioneered Dodge’s return to NASCAR. He served as the IOB’s secretary and treasurer last season.

Morgan has over five decades of global motorsport experience as a senior official, promoter, organizer and competitor. Morgan also is a member of the FIA World Motor Sport Council and advisor to the FIA president.

Both Nair and Evernham will continue with their specific leadership roles within the IOB in 2027. Nair has served as the IOB chairman and Evernham as its secretary and treasurer.

With the framework finalized in December 2025, INDYCAR established INDYCAR Officiating as an independent, not-for-profit organization to govern North America’s premier open-wheel racing series. As designed, the IOB is comprised of two members chosen via a vote from INDYCAR charter team owners, and the other member is appointed by the FIA. The IOB is charged with enforcement of INDYCAR and INDY NXT rules and establishing officiating and governance separation and process transparency for INDYCAR Officiating.

The IOB also has confirmed that veteran motorsports officiating and competition executive Scot Elkins will continue as INDYCAR Officiating’s managing director of officiating (MDO). Elkins was selected in April 2026 and began in May to oversee race control, race stewards and technical inspection. He will continue to report directly to the IOB – with no oversight from INDYCAR or Penske Entertainment Corp. officials – to provide officiating governance and management.

In June, Elkins instituted a formal three-steward model that will continue in 2027 and launched official post-event reports for both the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT by Firestone. The reports summarize race control activity, penalties, incident reviews and technical inspection findings, including matters reviewed and closed with no penalty. They are supported by published technical penalty guidelines carrying a three-level infraction framework, a central stewarding log and a precedent library, so that decisions can be measured against one another and provide a framework toward consistency across INDYCAR events. Post-event reports are available at https://noticeboard.indycarofficiating.org.

The IOB also worked closely with the FIA through its first season to exchange ideas and explore best practices. The FIA Officials Department assisted in the evaluation of stewarding practice and helped develop a more robust model. All three IOB members attended the FIA Formula One Miami Grand Prix to benchmark race control, stewarding, technical inspection and communications against Formula One and Formula 2. Additionally, FIA safety officials attended the Indianapolis 500 and met INDYCAR medical and rescue teams to learn how INDYCAR implements its medical and rescue operations, which remain under the direction and authority of INDYCAR.

WHAT THEY ARE SAYING:

“It was gratifying to see how well INDYCAR Officiating was integrated into the 2026 INDYCAR season, and I believe continuity of the IOB is important as it builds on the success from its first season. INDYCAR remains committed to clear independence in the application of our rulebook and the IOB is instrumental in that effort. Additionally, creating consistency in the rule enforcement and penalty guidelines is important to our teams, drivers and our fans, and I appreciate the IOB board’s leadership and Scot’s work in this area. ” – J. Douglas Boles, INDYCAR president

"We moved quickly but meticulously this year in instituting a more transparent process, enhanced by a formal three-steward model, technical penalty guidelines and post-event reports, which we believe has been beneficial for all of INDYCAR. With that foundation, several improvements land for the 2027 season: a rulebook review with INDYCAR, a clarified formal review and appeal process, and additional tools for race control. Alongside that, we are modernizing technical inspection, including scanning technology, with the aim of having it proven and in place before the IR-28 starts racing in 2028. Our entire INDYCAR Officiating team is buoyed by the support of the paddock and looks forward to getting started next season.” – Scot Elkins, INDYCAR Officiating managing director of officiating

“I maintain what I’ve said from the start – that INDYCAR already greatly benefited from the knowledgeable and professional officiating personnel in race control and technical inspection. Kyle Novak and Nick Allen lead tremendous teams, and I have been delighted to join and support them in my role. With Raj and Ronan, I look forward to continuing this journey of strengthening and adding another layer to an already skilled group.” – Ray Evernham, Independent Officiating Board secretary and treasurer

“I believed that this board would add another layer of experience and expertise to the process of INDYCAR Officiating, and with the quality of people who comprised that board, INDYCAR has, in fact, achieved that. I look forward to their continued participation relative to 2028 and the new IR-28 and corresponding rules and regulations.” – Chip Ganassi, Chip Ganassi Racing owner

“The implementation of the INDYCAR Officiating Board this past season was a pivotal step forward for the series to ensure fair and transparent processes and decision making across race control and tech inspection. The team and I were pleased with its effectiveness in 2026 and look forward to their continued leadership in 2027.” – Tony Kanaan, Arrow McLaren team principal

“Raj, Ray and Ronan have each brought valuable experience and perspective to their first year of service to INDYCAR Officiating, and unanimous support by the team owners has been proof of concept for the direction of independent officiating in our sport. With Scot Elkins continuing as the MDO in concert with the race control and tech inspection team already in place, officiating will build on the strong foundation and continue the mission of separation and transparency.” – Mark Miles, Penske Entertainment Corp. president and CEO

“I was pleased to see how seamlessly and successfully the established members of the team collaborated with the board to improve an already impressive product. INDYCAR Officiating is a sensible evolution and powerful way to support one of the best racing series in global motorsport. I expect 2027 will be another successful season of synergy and growth.” – Ronan Morgan, Independent Officiating Board member

“It has been a year of substantial growth for INDYCAR Officiating, and I would like to personally thank team owners, managers, drivers and partners for their unwavering support to our mission. Year two of INDYCAR Officiating will continue to build on our established baseline of process, independence, governance separation and transparency. We cannot wait to get started in the 2027 season.” – Raj Nair, Independent Officiating Board chairman

“The FIA is proud to continue our role on the INDYCAR Independent Officiating Board and to strengthen our partnership with INDYCAR and the wider motorsport community across the United States. This collaboration goes far beyond officiating – it is about sharing knowledge and expertise across safety, sporting integrity and governance, while learning from one another to deliver a stronger championship. I have been delighted to see this relationship grow over the past year and congratulate INDYCAR, its teams, drivers and officials on a historic 2026 season. We look forward to building on this momentum together in 2027.” – Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA president

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES and INDY NXT championships begin Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida. Coverage of the upcoming season will be provided by FOX, FOX Sports and INDYCAR Radio powered by OnlyBulls.

title: Gordon Johncock, 2-time Indy 500 winner, dies at 90
excerpt:
Gordon Johncock, a two-time Indianapolis 500 winner, died on Monday at his home in South Branch, Mich. He was 90.

He won the Indy 500 in 1973 and 1982 and finished with 25 victories, had 20 career poles and 76 podium finishes in open-wheel racing from 1964-83. He also made 21 starts in the NASCAR Cup Series in the 1960s and 1970s but was never a full-time driver.

At age 55, Johncock made his 24th and final start in the Indy 500 in 1992. Only A.J. Foyt, who was 57 for that same race in 1992, was older when he started the prestigious race.

Johncock was inducted into the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Hall of Fame in 1997, the International Motorsports Hall of Fame in 1999 and the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2002.

title: Ganassi Signs Christian Lundgaard To Drive No. 9 in Multiyear Deal
excerpt:
Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) has signed Danish driver Christian Lundgaard to a multiyear contract to drive the No. 9 PNC Bank Honda in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES starting in the 2027 season.

Three-time INDYCAR SERIES race winner Lundgaard (photo, above) has 16 podium finishes and 21 top-five finishes in 87 career starts. In 2026, he won races at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and at Road America, and he secured a career-best third-place finish in the INDYCAR SERIES championship standings.

Lundgaard will join teammates Alex Palou and Kyffin Simpson as part of the CGR’s 2027 driver lineup. He is replacing Scott Dixon, who left CGR after 24 full-time seasons and six series championships to join Arrow McLaren in 2027.

“It is an honor and a privilege to join Chip Ganassi Racing beginning next season,” Lundgaard said. “The fact that it is in the iconic No. 9 PNC Bank Honda makes it even more special. CGR has set the standard in INDYCAR for decades, and the opportunity to be part of that legacy is something I've worked toward my entire career.

“I'm incredibly excited about what's ahead. I can't wait to get to work with everyone at Chip Ganassi Racing and compete for wins, championships and the Indianapolis 500.”

Lundgaard, 25, has quickly become a well-rounded INDYCAR SERIES talent, scoring victories on both road and street circuits and scoring his first oval podium result in 2026. He was a winning driver in Formula 2 – one step below Formula One – and served briefly a simulator driver for the Alpine F1 Team before coming to the INDYCAR SERIES in 2021 with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. He earned his first victory in 2023 at Toronto with RLL before joining Arrow McLaren in 2025.

“We are excited to welcome Christian to Chip Ganassi Racing,” team owner Chip Ganassi said. “We know he's capable of accomplishing even more in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, and we're looking forward to helping him reach that next level with the No. 9 team.

“He's already proven he can win races, and it isn't often a driver of his caliber becomes available. Throughout our history, one of the things we've done best is identify young talent, help them maximize their potential and develop them into championship contenders. We believe Christian has all the talent to be the next driver to do that.”

PNC Bank will continue its longstanding partnership with CGR on the No. 9 PNC Bank Honda next season. PNC Bank has been a partner of the team since 2013 and a primary partner on the No. 9 since 2018. With approximately 2,300 branches and 58,000 employees, PNC is one of the largest financial institutions in the U.S.

“We are excited to begin a new era with Chip Ganassi Racing and what’s ahead with Christian taking the wheel of the No. 9 PNC Bank Honda,” said Lou Cestello, PNC Bank head of regional presidents. “He’s already achieved some remarkable milestones early in his career, and we’re looking forward to watching him build on that success in 2027 and beyond.”

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season starts Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.
